checks.name: E1-글로벌 이슈 현재성
checks.detail:
rank=2: outdated — Significantly understates the actual situation. Since Feb 28, 2026, the US and Israel have been in an active air war with Iran (Khamenei was killed), and the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively CLOSED to commercial shipping, not merely '35% reduced.' Late July data shows only ~10-13 tanker transits/day vs. ~88/day normal (an ~85-88% reduction), with IRGC laying mines and boarding vessels. The briefing's framing ('no new closure,' 'elevated naval presence') is stale/outdated relative to the current war footing.
    rank=3: inaccurate — No evidence of a unified GOOGL/META/MSFT/AAPL hearing with closing arguments due within 30 days. The four cases are actually at very different stages: Meta's FTC monopoly case was DISMISSED in Nov 2025 (judge ruled no monopoly power) and is now under FTC appeal to the DC Circuit, not in active remedies hearings. Google's case has remedies already issued (Sept 2025) with appeals expected late 2026/2027. Apple's DOJ case is pre-trial. Microsoft faces an ongoing FTC probe, not a hearing. The briefing's characterization of a single converging 'final phase' hearing across all four is not supported and appears fabricated/conflated.

global_issues.title: US-China chip export controls shift to case-by-case licensing + 25% tariff
global_issues.note: Confirmed: Jan 14-15, 2026 proclamation set 25% duty on Nvidia H200/AMD MI325X chips to China plus shift from presumption-of-denial to case-by-case licensing. Briefing omits one material detail: shipments are also capped at 50% of comparable US sales volume, and Nvidia's China AI chip market share has collapsed to near-zero despite the framework, per Jensen Huang (May 2026). Directionally correct but incomplete.

global_issues.title: Iran-Hormuz tanker traffic remains restricted amid elevated naval presence
global_issues.note: Significantly understates the actual situation. Since Feb 28, 2026, the US and Israel have been in an active air war with Iran (Khamenei was killed), and the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively CLOSED to commercial shipping, not merely '35% reduced.' Late July data shows only ~10-13 tanker transits/day vs. ~88/day normal (an ~85-88% reduction), with IRGC laying mines and boarding vessels. The briefing's framing ('no new closure,' 'elevated naval presence') is stale/outdated relative to the current war footing.

global_issues.title: DOJ/FTC AI antitrust remedies hearing enters final phase
global_issues.note: No evidence of a unified GOOGL/META/MSFT/AAPL hearing with closing arguments due within 30 days. The four cases are actually at very different stages: Meta's FTC monopoly case was DISMISSED in Nov 2025 (judge ruled no monopoly power) and is now under FTC appeal to the DC Circuit, not in active remedies hearings. Google's case has remedies already issued (Sept 2025) with appeals expected late 2026/2027. Apple's DOJ case is pre-trial. Microsoft faces an ongoing FTC probe, not a hearing. The briefing's characterization of a single converging 'final phase' hearing across all four is not supported and appears fabricated/conflated.

grok_report.summary: Stock prices and moves for AMZN, AAPL, and MU check out factually, and the VIX/market mood numbers are accurate. However, the briefing meaningfully understates the Strait of Hormuz crisis (it's an active war with the strait effectively closed, not '35% reduced with no closure') and appears to fabricate or badly conflate a unified DOJ/FTC AI antitrust 'final phase' hearing across GOOGL/META/MSFT/AAPL — Meta's case was actually dismissed in Nov 2025. The chip-tariff item is accurate but missing the volume-cap detail. A significant market-moving story (Chinese memory competitor CXMT's IPO driving the MU/chip selloff) is absent.
